<thought>To construct a single-step retrosynthesis, I will use the Peterson elimination. The target alkene (4,4'-dimethoxystilbene) can be traced back to a β‑hydroxy‑trimethylsilyl precursor: a carbon bearing a trimethylsilyl group and a hydroxyl group attached to the carbon that will become the other alkene carbon bearing the two para‑methoxy phenyl rings. This matches the forward Peterson reaction where a β‑hydroxy silane eliminates to give a C=C double bond while losing a trimethylsilyl group and an alcohol oxygen. I will locate a suitable retrosynthetic template for this transformation, then apply it to generate the precursor SMILES.</thought>
<action>search_template_catalog_by_criteria</action>
<action_input>{
  "molecule_smiles": "C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2",
  "functional_groups_broken": ["trimethylsilyl", "aliphatic hydroxyls"],
  "functional_groups_formed": ["C-C double bonds"],
  "limit": 10
}</action_input>
